method.driver: Chrome DevTools Protocol, runtime sampling every ~120 ms

findings.display_unit: a joined window of the source phrases that are active at that moment, not one raw source cue
findings.phrase_source: YouTube timed-text phrases (TTML p elements / json3 events) are pre-merged before display
findings.phrase_join: overlapping active phrases are concatenated into one source window; the shared tail is not de-duplicated
findings.translation_engine_seen: Microsoft Translator (loading label: 使用 微软翻译 翻译中...（沉浸式翻译）)

translation_latency_seconds.note: target line is empty or shows the loading label while the new source window is already visible

findings.reading_speed_trim: the pCe step shortens a phrase's display duration for reading speed; the source can change before the target finishes

ambient_filter.arrows: leading >> speaker markers are removed from the overlay source line
ambient_filter.evidence: native YouTube text contains '>> And when' and '[applause]'; overlay source text does not

findings.native_captions: the extension's own window is the visible caption in the captured screenshot; YouTube's caption container may still exist in the DOM
findings.native_word_highlight: YouTube's player can bold the current word in its own caption DOM; the extension overlay itself has no word-level highlight

limits: two short observation windows on one video, not a full-film comparison
the translation engine is identified from the overlay loading label, not from a captured network payload
the capture does not prove which internal function performs every merge; the source-code path was read separately
the observed windows are not a substitute for the committed seven-format caption corpus
